<!--
  PMS 1.43.3 GET /library/sections/{key}/all?type=4&unwatched=0 — the EPISODE-level watched read,
  which is the ground truth for what someone has watched in a TV library. Recorded 2026-09-01 from a
  real server (plex-safety rule 11). Titles and ids are sanitized; attribute NAMES, the container
  shape and the presence/absence of each attribute are verbatim.

  WHY THIS FIXTURE EXISTS — issue #108. It is BOTH the evidence for the query the show read now
  sends (reasoning that is not reconstructable from the code) and the recorded shape of a read
  production makes again: `_newest_episode_stamps` walks this exact endpoint to date a show whose own
  row carries no `lastViewedAt`. Its `totalSize` of 9563 is also the measurement behind that
  function's per-page fold — retaining these rows instead cost ~14MB per user per library per sync.

  `?type=2&unwatched=0` asks Plex about the SHOW row, and that row can disagree with its own
  episodes. Measured on a real server, same library, same admin token, on the same day:

    ?type=2&unwatched=0        ->   533 shows
    ?type=2                    ->  4880 shows, of which 491 have viewedLeafCount > 0
    ?type=2&viewedLeafCount!=0 ->   491 shows
    ?type=4&unwatched=0        ->  9563 episodes, rolling up to exactly those same 491 shows

  and **20 of those 491 never came back from `?type=2&unwatched=0` at all.** Inspected individually,
  every one of them looks like this:

      eps_watched=38  viewedLeafCount=38  leafCount=38  lastViewedAt=None
      eps_watched=6   viewedLeafCount=6   leafCount=6   lastViewedAt=None
      eps_watched=2   viewedLeafCount=2   leafCount=20  lastViewedAt=None

  So `unwatched=0` on `type=2` filters on the show's own `lastViewedAt`/watch-state row, NOT on
  `viewedLeafCount` — and a show whose show-level row was never established is invisible to it while
  its episode counts are perfectly correct. Marking a series or a season watched is one way to end up
  there; the reporter of #108 found that marking a single episode BY HAND establishes the row and the
  whole show then appears.

  The episode roll-up below was the FIRST fix: walk the episodes and rebuild the shows from them. It
  worked (533 -> 552 on the live server, 0 lost) and was then replaced by `viewedLeafCount!=0`, which
  the reporter suggested and which returns the identical 491 in one read at half the cost — 0
  missing and 0 extra against this episode-derived truth, in both directions. The rows below record
  the shape that measurement was taken from.

  A TRAP, recorded because it cost a wrong diagnosis: you cannot look for these shows by asking
  `?type=2&unwatched=0` which of its rows lack `lastViewedAt`. That query EXCLUDES them by
  definition, so the answer is always zero and reads like proof they do not exist.
-->
